answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a stake-and-reputation ledger modeled on an atlas of verified work. Each agent must lock a bond and build a public history of completed jobs; new identities start in a narrow canyon of low-trust tasks and only earn wider access by delivering value. Creating a fake identity costs the bond plus the time to climb out of the canyon, while a single proven identity earns a saffron badge that unlocks premium work. Attackers must pay the bond for every fake, so mass-producing identities becomes unprofitable while honest agents compound trust.
